quick.summary: Why last year’s report changed by itself, and how to keep the past.
quick.takeaway: Add a new row with dates. Keep the old one.

beats.line: A customer moved city. Now last year’s sales by city look different. Why?
You replaced the old city. The past now uses the new one.
But the new city is the correct one.
Correct today. Last year’s sales happened in the old city.
So keep both. Add a new row when a value changes.
Each row says when it was true. From which date, to which date.
A sale then joins to the row that was true on its date.
Two rows for that customer, each with its dates.
Now last year stays last year.

quiz.question: A customer changes city. How do you keep past reports correct?
options: Add a new row with the dates each city was valid
Overwrite the city with the new one
Delete the customer and add them again
quiz.explanation: Rows with valid dates let each sale join to the city that was true when it happened.

quiz.question: Overwriting a changed value keeps past reports the same.
quiz.explanation: It changes how the past is reported, because old records now pick up the new value.
